title: Розыгрыш для Кати  (A Prank on Katya)

segments.t: At home late at night, Nastya wakes up with a sudden craving, while the next morning in the locker room Senya and Fedya plant a fake mouse in Katya's locker to scare her.
Но штуку я всё равно выиграл.
Now let's go back through their conversation line by line and unpack the Russian phrasing.
'Well, blow me down!' Senya counters steadily hearing Kostya, without trying to dress up how he really feels.
'I left it myself, I don't remember where.' Senya reaches for one direct term right here: "ostavila" means "left" (from "ostavit"), giving the line its exact edge.
'Nastya, where are you?' Kostya delivers the thought with ease: notice how Russian needs no word for "am", "is", or "are" in the present — placing the words side by side says it all.
'I felt like having a little apple.' Nastya holds firm pointedly with Senya, without trying to dress up how she really feels.
'Let me peel it.' Kostya points to one concrete word with Nastya: "pochishchu" means "will peel, clean" (from "pochistit"), giving the line its exact edge.
'No, go to sleep.' Nastya states that point in earnest: spoken Russian trims this down to just 3 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
'They brought him that fugu fish.' Senya speaks quietly to be clear, before Kostya can change the subject.
'He ate it and died.' Senya sharpens one pointed term in earnest: "pomer" means "died" (from "pomeret"), giving the line its exact edge.
'Then it turned out to be a stroke.' Senya puts this answer with candor: the "-sya" ending on "okazalsya" ("turned up") turns the action inward or makes it happen between people naturally.
Но штуку я всё равно выиграл.
'But I still won a grand anyway.' Senya answers frankly without any doubt, bringing things back to earth after the buildup.
'Hand it over!' Senya stresses one memorable word for Kostya: "otday" means "give back" (from "otdat"), giving the line its exact edge.
'Nicely done!' Kostya gives the remark before Senya: spoken Russian trims this down to just 1 words, dropping the extra helper words that English has to spell out.
Но штуку я всё равно выиграл.
And that finishes Scene Three. Listen out for Nastya's late-night apple excuse and Senya's tall tale about the fugu fish bet. Until next time!
